newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Patten pooch narrowly escapes HK dog poisoner.
newsitem.headline: Patten pooch narrowly escapes HK dog poisoner.

text.p: One of Governor Chris Patten's two Norfolk terriers narrowly escaped death at the hands of Hong Kong's notorious "Bowen Road Dog poisoner."
The governor's wife, Lavender, wrote to the English-language South China Morning Post on Tuesday to suggest dog owners muzzle their pets.

She said the two dogs, Whisky and Soda, were leashed when she took them out for a walk along a popular trail on Hong Kong island but Whisky managed to snaffle a piece of chicken later found to have been soaked in an insecticide-type poison.
Whisky survived but several other pets have not been so lucky, she wrote.
She urged passersby to watch out for anyone acting suspiciously and report them to the police.
"Who knows, one day a child may be affected," she wrote.
The Pattens' dogs have been a source of constant amusement to Chinese political cartoonists and often make the headlines in Hong Kong.
